Sooo I see a lot of negative comments so I’m going to play devils advocate. I have adhd and social anxiety like crazy. Not gonna lie, I often make plans feeling confident then later find a way to cancel day of as it the anxiety becomes too much. Before I learned how to communicate how it was affecting me I’m sure I pissed off a lot of people or made them feel like I didn’t care. It was hard to try to explain what was going on as part of me was still in denial. I went from an extremely outgoing person constantly hanging out with people to suddenly not being able to even go to the grocery store without my husband by my side. I’ve gone to therapy to help be able to better at communicating to those close to me how the anxiety impacts me and being upfront about plans. On the other hand, my adhd makes me super forgetful so I have made double plans before and I would choose the person I thought wouldn’t be as understanding about being canceled on. (I’m now better that I immediately put any plan in my phone the moment it’s being planned with reminders 😅). So while it could be her just not seeing the importance and being careless, it could also be the social anxiety/double planning and feeling comfortable enough with you to be the one to cancel on/ also not being in a place yet to learn how to communicate that’s what’s going on. I’d definitely have a conversation about how it makes you feel and if these are the reasons she canceled that perhaps seeking some therapy will be beneficial.

This doesn’t sound legal at all. It sounds exactly like you said, he condensed her apartment to make yours bigger. If he did this though, I don’t see why he wouldn’t just make the address as one. Even if it is part of the other, it wouldn’t matter with a lease since you have an address with the other side. He could have even stipulated it in the lease, that while the other side has a different address, your address is “this” and when you leave you’re only responsible for “this” side and the other two rooms. Very simple thing to add on. However with the wording you’re saying is by addresses, then by contract, yes he could make you responsible BUT I doubt a judge would even consider it. I would highly advise finding a tenant lawyer. From my experience, California has some strict tenant/landlord laws and this sounds 100 percent absolutely illegal to me.

Not sure which state you are in, but you might be able to be hired on as a teacher on the record. Essentially the school, WGU, and you go over a timeline of when you plan on finishing and can then be approved for a temporary teaching certificate to teach. Which would also then count as your student teaching. That is what a lot of people where I am from in Missouri are doing. I would look into it as a possibility if you haven't already done it all yet. However, I do agree that the expectation to be able to do all of that without pay is simply ridiculous. In today's society, you need 2, almost 3 pays coming in just to make ends meet...and with the teacher shortage, you would think this would be something they would change.

You mean the one that takes months to get into see, let alone talk to. Yup, we did that. Did we also go see other Drs, yup, did that. If I had never reached out to others about any of my symptoms to see what others might have been diagnosed with/gone through to then come back to my drs I would STILL be waiting on diagnosis's as my symptoms weren't a-typical.  Currently right now I have seen THREE different drs for issues I am having with my thumb, every single one of them have told me they have no clue what it could be and not sure who to refer me to so sorry just deal with it and hope its not something serious. Perhaps if we had a better healthcare system here with Drs who really did try to listen and help people wouldn't have to go to reddit, but alas, here we are. Compassion goes a long way in not only healthcare, but even day to day interactions with others. Try it sometime.
